skill.name: Reward Formulation via Policy-Reference Log Ratio
skill.description: Compute implicit reward signals using the log ratio of likelihood between a current policy model and a supervised fine-tuned reference model. This micro-skill eliminates the need for an explicit reward model in preference-based learning by directly scoring response pairs.
skill.skill_body:
Calculate the implicit reward for a response pair by taking the log ratio of the likelihood under the current policy model to the likelihood under the supervised fine-tuned reference model. Use this scalar reward to score preference comparisons without training a separate reward model.

## Objective

Compute implicit reward signal from model likelihood ratios without explicit reward model
## Applicable Signals

- Preference labels between response pairs
- Current policy model likelihood estimates
- Supervised fine-tuned reference model likelihood estimates

## Contraindications

- Reward function must be human-interpretable or auditable
- Explicit reward model already available and preferred for other pipeline stages
- Likelihood estimates are unreliable or model outputs are unstable

## Workflow Steps

- Obtain likelihood of response under current policy model
- Obtain likelihood of same response under supervised fine-tuned reference model
- Compute log ratio: log(P_policy / P_reference)
- Return scalar reward score for preference pair

## Constraints

- Both policy and reference model must be available and comparable
- Likelihood estimates must be computed on the same response samples
- Log ratio computation requires valid probability values from both models

## Cautions

- Implicit reward formulation may not align directly with human preference intent in all domains
- Numerical stability of log ratios depends on model calibration

## Output Contract

- Scalar reward score per response pair that correlates with human preference labels; suitable for downstream preference optimization steps
